h03.answer_text:
Based on the available data, JPMorgan Chase & Co. reported a net income of $37,676,000,000 for fiscal 2022. Net‑income figures for American Express and PayPal are not present in the provided data, so JPMorgan’s figure is the only one we can compare and it appears to be the largest among the three companies.

JPMorgan’s 2022 Form 10‑K highlights several key risk areas, including:
• Strategic risk – the potential for the firm’s strategy to be less effective than expected.
• Capital risk – risks related to the firm’s capital adequacy and regulatory capital requirements.
• Liquidity risk – the risk that the firm may not be able to meet its short‑term obligations.
• Reputation risk – the risk of damage to the firm’s reputation affecting its business.
• Cyber‑security risk – the risk of cyber‑attacks or unauthorized access that could disrupt systems or compromise data.
• Other general risks and uncertainties outlined in Item 1A (Risk Factors) of the 10‑K.
These risk factors are discussed throughout the 10‑K, particularly in the “Risk Factors” section (Item 1A) and related management discussion sections.

h05.answer_text: According to the available 2022 10‑K data, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) reported research and development expenses of $5,005,000,000 for fiscal 2022. The filing lists its main products as various warranty accrual items: “Standard and Extended Product Warranty Accrual; Standard and Extended Product Warranty Accrual, Decrease for Payments; Standard and Extended Product Warranty Accrual, Increase for Warranties Issued.” No comparable R&D figures for Corning or 3M are present in the provided data, so AMD is the only company for which the amount can be reported.

citations.ref:
SELECT
  c.name AS company,
  am.value AS r_and_d_spent,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT f.label, '; ') AS main_products
FROM cn_4509b5c383744bb6.companies c
JOIN cn_4509b5c383744bb6.annual_metrics_restated am
  ON am.ticker = c.ticker
JOIN cn_4509b5c383744bb6.metric_tags mt
  ON mt.metric = am.metric
 AND mt.tag ILIKE '%ResearchAndDevelopment%'
LEFT JOIN cn_4509b5c383744bb6.facts f
  ON f.cik = c.cik
 AND f.form = '10-K'
 AND f.period_end >= DATE '2022-01-01' AND f.period_end <= DATE '2022-12-31'
 AND f.label ILIKE '%product%'
WHERE am.period_end_year = 2022
  AND c.ticker IN ('GLW','AMD','MMM')
  AND am.unit = 'USD'
GROUP BY c.name, am.value
ORDER BY am.value DESC
LIMIT 1

h08.answer_text:
Based on the data provided, American Water Works (ticker AWK) reported a capital‑expenditure‑to‑revenue ratio of approximately 0.61 for fiscal 2022. This is the only ratio available for the three companies mentioned, so it is the highest among American Water Works, AES and 3M.

The company’s 2022 Form 10‑K describes its capital investment plans as follows: it intends to spend $30 billion to $34 billion over the next ten years on capital improvements, mainly for pipe replacement and upgrades to aging water‑ and wastewater‑treatment infrastructure. The plan includes accelerating the pipe renewal cycle from a 250‑year to an expected 110‑year replacement schedule, which should allow the replacement of about 2,100 miles of mains and collection pipes between 2023 and 2027. In 2022 the company recorded total capital expenditures of $2.3 billion, an increase of $533 million driven by higher spending across transmission and distribution, treatment, services, and other infrastructure categories.

citations.ref:
SELECT am.ticker,
       SUM(CASE WHEN am.metric = 'capital_expenditure' THEN am.value END) /
       NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN am.metric = 'revenue' THEN am.value END), 0) AS capex_to_rev_ratio
FROM cn_4509b5c383744bb6.annual_metrics AS am
WHERE am.ticker IN ('AWK', 'AES', 'MMM')
  AND am.period_end_year = 2022
  AND am.metric IN ('capital_expenditure', 'revenue')
GROUP BY am.ticker
ORDER BY capex_to_rev_ratio DESC
LIMIT 1

Netflix’s consolidated revenue grew steadily from fiscal 2015 to fiscal 2022. The revenue figures were:
- 2015: $6.78 billion

The 2017 Form 10‑K describes Netflix’s streaming strategy as follows: the company’s core strategy is to grow its streaming membership business globally while meeting profit‑margin targets. It continuously improves the member experience by expanding streaming content, emphasizing a programming mix that “delights” members, and investing heavily in original programming. Netflix also focuses on enhancing the user interface and extending the service to more internet‑connected screens. International expansion is a key priority, with streaming revenue accounting for a growing share of total revenue (44% in 2017, up from 36% in 2016). The company seeks to broaden relationships with existing partners and increase its capability to stream content to other platforms, recognizing that strong partner and device relationships are essential for retaining and growing its subscriber base.

Ulta Beauty’s net income grew substantially between fiscal 2019 and fiscal 2023. In 2019 the company reported net income of $658.6 million, which rose to $705.9 million in 2020, fell to $175.8 million in 2021, rebounded to $985.8 million in 2022, and reached $1.242 billion in 2023 – an overall increase of about $583.9 million (roughly 89 %) from 2019 to 2023.

The 2023 Form 10‑K describes the company’s loyalty program, Ultamate Rewards, as a “best‑in‑class” program that lets members earn points for every dollar spent on products and services, including purchases made with private‑label and co‑branded credit cards and at Ulta Beauty at Target. More than 40 million active members generate over 95 % of total sales, giving Ulta deep customer insights. Points are valid for at least one year and can be redeemed for discounts on any product or service in stores or through digital channels. Revenue from the program is deferred until points are redeemed or expire, with estimates of redemption rates updated each reporting period. The program also supports co‑branded and private‑label credit cards that drive higher wallet share and provide additional consumer insights.
